en: to be viewed across; to be seen across

examples.ko: 우리 집 창문에서 강 건너 마을이 건너다보여요.
examples.en: From my window I can see the village across the river.

examples.ko: 맑은 날에는 바다 건너 섬이 건너다보였어요.
examples.en: On a clear day, the island across the sea was visible.
If you go up to the rooftop, you can see the apartment building opposite.
I can see a small temple on the far side of the lake.
The night view you can see across from the balcony is really pretty.

examples.ko: 이 방은 이웃집이 건너다보여서 커튼을 달았어요.
examples.en: You can see the neighbor's house from this room, so I put up a curtain.

explain: 멀리 맞은편에 있는 것이 눈에 들어올 때 써요. 그냥 '보이다'와 달리 강, 길, 호수처럼 사이에 건너야 할 거리가 있다는 느낌이 있어요. 내가 일부러 바라보는 것은 '건너다보다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The mountain visible across the way from the window is beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 건너편에 보이는 풍경을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form for scenery visible on the far side.

phrases.example: 안개가 껴서 강 건너편이 건너다보이지 않아요.
phrases.en: It's foggy, so I can't see the other side of the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨나 거리 때문에 맞은편이 잘 안 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the other side can't be seen due to weather or distance.

phrases.en: I looked across the street at the shop from the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건너다보이다'는 저절로 보이는 것이고, '건너다보다'는 내가 일부러 바라보는 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '건너다보이다' is what comes into view; '건너다보다' is looking on purpose.

explain_en: It is used when something far on the opposite side comes into view. Unlike plain '보이다', it suggests something like a river, road or lake lies in between. When you look on purpose, the verb is '건너다보다'.

examples.ko: 설 연휴 마지막 날은 오후부터 귀경하는 차들 때문에 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: On the last day of the Lunar New Year holiday, traffic jams from the afternoon because of cars heading back to Seoul.

examples.ko: 부모님이 챙겨 주신 반찬을 들고 귀경했어요.
examples.en: I headed back to Seoul carrying the side dishes my parents packed for me.

examples.ko: 연휴가 끝나기 전에 일찍 귀경하려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm planning to head back to Seoul early, before the holiday ends.

examples.ko: 저는 일요일 저녁에 귀경해서 월요일에 바로 출근했어요.
examples.en: I returned to Seoul on Sunday evening and went straight to work on Monday.

examples.ko: 귀경한 뒤에도 고향 음식 생각이 자꾸 나요.
examples.en: Even after returning to Seoul, I keep thinking about my hometown food.

examples.ko: 길이 막히는 게 싫어서 새벽에 귀경했어요.
examples.en: I hate traffic jams, so I went back to Seoul at dawn.

explain: 명절이나 휴가에 고향에 갔다가 서울로 돌아오는 것을 말하고, 뉴스에서 '귀경길 정체'처럼 많이 나와요. 반대로 고향에 가는 것은 '귀성'이고, 평소 대화에서는 '서울로 올라오다'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The highway gets very congested on the way back to Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명절 뒤 서울로 돌아오는 길을 말하고 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The road back to Seoul after a holiday; often heard in the news.

phrases.en: The holiday is over, so I'm coming back up to Seoul today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀경하다'보다 평소 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in everyday conversation than 귀경하다.

phrases.example: 귀경객이 한꺼번에 몰려서 저녁까지 길이 막혀요.
phrases.en: Travelers returning to Seoul come all at once, so the road is jammed until evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명절 뒤 서울로 돌아오는 사람들을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to people returning to Seoul after a holiday.

explain_en: It means coming back to Seoul after visiting your hometown during a holiday or vacation, and it often appears in the news as '귀경길 정체' (traffic jam on the way back). The opposite, going to your hometown, is '귀성', and in everyday talk people often say '서울로 올라오다'.

en: to be all-around; to be multi-talented; to be a jack-of-all-trades

examples.ko: 제 친구는 노래도 잘하고 그림도 잘 그리는 다재다능한 사람이에요.
examples.en: My friend is a multi-talented person who sings well and draws well.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 연기도 하고 작곡도 해서 정말 다재다능해요.
examples.en: That actor acts and also composes music, so he is really versatile.

examples.ko: 다재다능하면 어떤 일을 맡아도 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: If you are versatile, you don't have to worry whatever job you take on.

examples.ko: 다재다능하다는 말을 자주 듣지만 저는 제대로 잘하는 게 없어요.
examples.en: People often call me talented in many ways, but I'm not really good at any one thing.
She is a singer who is active in many fields with versatile talent.
I heard that teacher was multi-talented even when he was young.

explain: 여러 분야에서 재능이 있는 사람을 칭찬할 때 쓰고, 주로 사람을 꾸며서 '다재다능한 사람'처럼 말해요. '만능'이나 '팔방미인'과도 비슷하게 쓰여요. 물건이 아니라 사람에게 쓰는 말이라는 점에 주의해요.

phrases.en: My older brother is multi-talented.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite spoken form for praising a person.

phrases.example: 그는 팔방미인이라 못 하는 게 없어요.
phrases.en: He is good at everything, so there's nothing he can't do.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 방면에 능한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person skilled in many areas.

phrases.en: That friend can do everything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '다재다능하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say someone is multi-talented.

explain_en: It is used to praise someone with talent in many areas, usually describing a person, as in '다재다능한 사람'. It is used similarly to '만능' and '팔방미인'. Note that it is for people, not objects.

en: to be smooth; to be sleek

examples.ko: 새로 산 책상 표면이 정말 매끈해요.
examples.en: The surface of the new desk is really smooth.
I envy that smooth face like a baby's skin.

examples.ko: 길이 매끈하게 포장되어 있어서 걷기 편했어요.
examples.en: The road was smoothly paved, so it was comfortable to walk on.
That car had a sleek design.
If you grind the stone for a long time, it will become smooth.
That actor has a sleek, slim figure.

explain: '부드럽다'는 만졌을 때 순한 느낌이고, 매끈하다는 걸리는 데 없이 반들반들한 느낌이에요. '매끄럽다'는 일이 막힘없이 진행될 때 더 자주 쓰고, 매끈하다는 주로 피부, 돌, 도로, 차 디자인처럼 겉면과 모양에 써요.

phrases.en: I picked up a smooth stone by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 겉면이 반들반들한 것을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a glossy, even surface before a noun.

phrases.en: I sanded the wooden box until it was smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 결과가 매끈하다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a verb, it adds the meaning that the result is smooth.

phrases.example: 이 길은 매끈하지 않아서 걷기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: This road is not smooth, so it is hard to walk on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표면이 울퉁불퉁하다는 뜻을 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the surface is bumpy.

explain_en: 부드럽다 is a gentle, soft feel, while 매끈하다 is a shiny surface with nothing that catches. 매끄럽다 is used more often for things going smoothly, while 매끈하다 is mainly for surfaces and shapes such as skin, stone, roads, and car design.

examples.ko: 콘서트 표가 십 분 만에 매진됐어요.
examples.en: The concert tickets sold out in ten minutes.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 빵은 오전에 다 매진돼요.
examples.en: The popular bread sells out completely in the morning.

examples.ko: 영화 표가 매진돼서 다음 시간으로 봤어요.
examples.en: The movie tickets were sold out, so we watched the next showing.

examples.ko: 신제품이 출시 하루 만에 매진되었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the new product sold out within a day of its release.
Book quickly before it sells out.

examples.ko: 벌써 매진된 공연이라 표를 못 구했어요.
examples.en: It was a show that had already sold out, so I could not get a ticket.

explain: 표나 상품이 모두 팔렸을 때 써요. 가게 앞이나 예매 사이트에서 '매진'이라는 글자를 자주 볼 수 있어요. 물건이 다 떨어졌을 때는 '품절'이라고도 하는데, 공연·영화·기차표에는 '매진', 상품에는 '품절'을 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The train tickets are already sold out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연, 영화, 기차표가 다 팔렸을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when concert, movie, or train tickets are all sold.

phrases.en: Today's show is sold out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매진'이라는 명사로 지금 상태를 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '매진' to state the current situation briefly.

phrases.en: That bag is out of stock right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표보다 상품이 다 떨어졌을 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more for products than tickets that have run out.

explain_en: Used when tickets or goods have all been sold. You often see '매진' posted at shops and booking sites. '품절' also means out of stock, but 매진 is more common for shows, movies, and train tickets, while 품절 is more common for products.

examples.en: Children aged 6 and under get free admission.
On Sundays the museum has free admission, so it's crowded.

examples.ko: 학생증을 보여 주면 무료입장을 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you show your student ID, you can get in for free.
By any chance, is today's event free to enter?
Free admission starts at five in the afternoon.
The poster said 'free admission', so I went in.

explain: 안내문과 광고에서 많이 보는 말이고, '입장 무료'라고도 써요. 말로 할 때는 '무료로 들어가다'나 '공짜로 들어가다'도 써요. 반대는 돈을 내고 들어가는 '유료'예요.

phrases.en: Admission is free for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무료입장'과 순서만 다르고 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '무료입장' with the word order reversed.

phrases.example: 학생증이 있으면 무료로 들어갈 수 있어요.
phrases.en: With a student ID you can get in for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로 설명할 때 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural way to say it in conversation.

phrases.en: There is a free admission event this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사나 광고에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in event notices and ads.

explain_en: It is common on notices and ads and is also written '입장 무료'. In speech you can say '무료로 들어가다' or the casual '공짜로 들어가다'. The opposite is '유료', where you pay to enter.

examples.en: Please mix the rice evenly with the rice paddle.
Rice grains keep sticking to the rice paddle.

examples.ko: 밥주걱을 물에 적시면 밥이 덜 붙어요.
examples.en: If you wet the rice paddle, the rice sticks less.
I needed a new rice paddle, so I went to the mart.
I bought a rice paddle.
This rice paddle is plastic, so it's light and easy to use.

explain: 밥솥에서 밥을 푸고 섞을 때 쓰는 도구예요. 줄여서 그냥 '주걱'이라고도 하고, 국을 뜨는 도구는 '국자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I scoop the rice with a paddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밥주걱'을 줄여서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 밥주걱.

phrases.en: I'm scooping rice with the rice paddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 그릇에 담는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes serving rice into a bowl.
phrases.en_equiv: to scoop rice with a paddle

phrases.en: After eating, I wash the rice paddle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥알이 붙어 있어서 바로 씻는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often washed right away because rice sticks to it.

explain_en: It is the tool you use to scoop and mix rice from the rice cooker. It is often shortened to just '주걱', and the tool for ladling soup is called '국자'.

examples.en: We take the exam in the library annex.
The annex is behind the main building.
The meeting is held on the third floor of the annex.
A new restaurant opened in the annex.
Please enter through the annex entrance instead of the main building.
Please tell me the way to the annex.

explain: 별관은 중심 건물 옆에 따로 지은 건물이고, 중심 건물은 '본관'이라고 해요. '신관'이나 '동관'처럼 이름이 붙은 건물도 많아요. 학교, 병원, 호텔에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I have class, so I'm going to the annex.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 건물로 이동한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving to the separate building.

phrases.en: The main building and the annex are connected by a bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 건물을 함께 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to speak of the two buildings together.

phrases.en: I take the exam on the third floor of the annex.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별관의 몇 층인지 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which floor of the annex something is on.

explain_en: 별관 is a building built separately beside the main one, which is called 본관. Buildings also carry names like 신관 or 동관. You see these at schools, hospitals, and hotels.

examples.en: There is a big fountain in the middle of the park.

examples.ko: 주말에는 분수대 앞에서 약속을 많이 해요.
examples.en: On weekends, many people arrange to meet in front of the fountain.
Children are running around the fountain.

examples.ko: 여름에는 분수대에서 시원한 물이 뿜어져 나와요.
examples.en: In summer, cool water sprays out of the fountain.

examples.ko: 분수대로 가는 길이 공사 때문에 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road to the fountain is blocked because of construction.

examples.ko: 저녁에 분수대에 불이 켜지면 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: When the lights come on at the fountain in the evening, it is really pretty.

explain: 뿜어 나오는 물줄기는 '분수', 그 물이 나오는 시설이나 그 자리는 '분수대'라고 해요. '분수대 앞에서 만나요'처럼 약속 장소로 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 분수대 앞에서 오후 세 시에 만나요.
phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the fountain at three in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 정할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for setting a meeting spot.

phrases.en: The fountain's water shot high into the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분수'는 물줄기이고 '분수대'는 그 시설이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 분수 is the jet of water; 분수대 is the structure.

phrases.en: I sat and rested on the bench next to the fountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변 위치를 말할 때 '옆'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combine with 옆 to describe a nearby spot.
phrases.en_equiv: the bench next to the fountain

explain_en: The spray of water itself is '분수', while the structure or the spot where it is located is '분수대'. People often use it as a meeting place, as in '분수대 앞에서 만나요'.

examples.en: My friends sat in a circle around the table.
I went all the way around the park and broke a sweat.
The kids gathered in a ring around the teacher.

examples.ko: 집 주변에 나무를 삥 둘러 심었어요.
examples.en: We planted trees in a ring around the house.

examples.ko: 갑자기 어지러워서 방이 삥 도는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I suddenly felt dizzy, as if the room were spinning.

examples.ko: 길을 몰라서 같은 동네를 삥 돌아서 왔어요.
examples.en: I didn't know the way, so I came around the same neighborhood in a loop.

explain: 둥글게 한 바퀴 도는 모양이나 빙 둘러서 있는 모양에 써요. '빙'보다 조금 센 느낌이 있어요. 어지러울 때는 '핑 돌다'를 더 흔히 써요.

phrases.en: The children stood in a circle around the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 한 곳을 둥글게 둘러싸고 서 있는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many people standing in a ring around one spot.

phrases.en: I went around the playground and then went home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 바퀴 크게 도는 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes going around once in a big loop.

phrases.en: People surrounded the singer in a ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 사람이나 물건을 빙 둘러서 에워쌀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people or things form a ring around someone or something.

explain_en: It describes going once around in a circle or standing in a ring. It feels slightly stronger than '빙'. For dizziness, '핑 돌다' is more common.

en: to be strange; to be odd

examples.en: This food smells a bit odd.
I heard a strange sound and looked behind me.
Since yesterday the machine has been acting weird.
That person's outfit looked strange.
I thought it looked odd, but it tasted good when I tried it.

examples.ko: 꿈이 너무 요상해서 친구한테 얘기해 줬어요.
examples.en: My dream was so weird that I told my friend about it.

explain: '이상하다'보다 입말 느낌이 강하고, 조금 장난스럽거나 못마땅한 느낌이 들어요. 글이나 발표보다 편한 대화에서 어울려요. '요상한 + 명사', '요상하게 + 동사'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: There is a strange smell from the kitchen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 가장 기본적인 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic form for describing a noun.

phrases.en: That fruit has a strange shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'로 바꿔서 뒤의 동사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Changes to '-게' to describe the verb that follows.

phrases.en: The taste isn't as strange as I thought.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 '이상하지 않다'는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form means 'not strange'.

explain_en: It feels more colloquial than '이상하다' and can sound a bit playful or disapproving. It fits casual conversation better than writing or presentations. It is often used as '요상한 + noun' or '요상하게 + verb'.

examples.ko: 방바닥이 절절 끓어서 앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The floor is boiling hot, so it's hard to sit.
In winter, an ondol room is best when the floor is piping hot.
I lay down on the scorching floor at the sauna.

examples.ko: 아랫목이 절절 끓어서 이불 속이 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The warmest spot of the room is so hot that it's cozy under the blanket.

examples.ko: 보일러를 세게 틀었더니 바닥이 절절 끓어요.
examples.en: I turned the boiler up high, and now the floor is blazing hot.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 아랫목은 늘 절절 끓었어요.
examples.en: The warmest spot in Grandma's house was always scorching hot.

explain: 주로 '절절 끓다'로 방바닥이 아주 뜨거울 때 써요. '절절하다'와 소리는 비슷하지만 감정을 말하는 게 아니라 뜨거운 느낌을 말해요.

phrases.en: In winter the warmest spot on the floor is boiling hot and cozy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 온돌방에서 가장 따뜻한 자리가 아주 뜨거울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the warmest spot of a heated floor is very hot.

phrases.en: I rested well in the piping hot room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절절 끓다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The floor is nice and hot, so I feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '절절'보다 덜 강하고 기분 좋게 따뜻한 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gentler than '절절' and suggests a pleasant warmth.

explain_en: It is mainly used as '절절 끓다' when a floor is extremely hot. It sounds similar to '절절하다', but it describes heat, not emotion.

en: tactlessness; lack of discretion; acting out of place (esp. for one's age)

examples.en: Please don't tease me for acting silly at my age.
Dad embarrassed me again by acting out of line.
Crying all of a sudden, I am being silly.

examples.ko: 할머니는 주책없이 큰 소리로 노래를 부르셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother sang loudly without any sense of occasion.

examples.ko: 회식에서 주책 부리는 상사 때문에 민망했어요.
examples.en: I felt awkward because my boss was acting inappropriately at the company dinner.
Everyone laughed because of the silly behavior.

explain: 상황이나 나이에 맞지 않게 말하고 행동하는 모습을 가볍게 놀리거나 흉볼 때 써요. '주책이다', '주책을 떨다', '주책 부리다'처럼 쓰고, '주책없다'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm being tactless again, I'm sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 행동을 부끄러워하며 말할 때 써요. 남에게 쓰면 흉보는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feeling embarrassed about your own behavior. About others, it sounds like teasing.

phrases.en: Tears are coming out at the wrong time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주책'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '주책없이'로 행동 앞에 자주 붙어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 주책. Often appears as 주책없이 before an action.

phrases.en: Please don't act out of place at the company dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황에 맞지 않게 행동한다는 뜻이에요. '주책을 떨다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means acting in a way that doesn't fit the situation. Similar to 주책을 떨다.

explain_en: It is used to lightly tease or criticize someone who talks or acts in a way that does not fit the situation or their age. It appears as '주책이다', '주책을 떨다', and '주책 부리다', and '주책없다' is very often used with almost the same meaning.

examples.en: I got paid, so I'll treat you today.
I treated my team members to celebrate my promotion.
If you passed, you have to treat us!
My friend got a job and decided to treat us.
The person who treats is the one who pays.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 제가 점심 한턱낼 테니 오세요.
examples.en: I'll treat you to lunch this weekend, so come over.

explain: 좋은 일이 있을 때 다른 사람들에게 음식이나 술자리 등을 대접하는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '한턱 쏘다'라고도 해요. 그냥 밥값을 나눠 내는 것과 달리 한 사람이 기쁨을 나누며 사는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Today I'll treat everyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이라 친구나 동료에게 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken expression that suits friends and coworkers.

phrases.en: If I pass the test, I'll treat you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 대접하겠다고 약속할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to promise that you will treat someone.

phrases.en: You got a job, so you should treat us!
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 일이 생긴 사람에게 대접해 달라고 장난스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Playfully asking someone with good news to treat everyone.

explain_en: It means to treat others to a meal or outing when something good happens. In speech people also say '한턱 쏘다'. Unlike splitting the bill, it feels like one person paying to share their happiness.

en: to get a windfall; to strike it rich

examples.en: I found ten thousand won on the street, what a windfall.
Winning the lottery, you really struck it rich.

examples.ko: 중고 가게에서 새 책을 싸게 사서 횡재한 기분이에요.
examples.en: I bought a new book cheaply at a used shop and feel like I got a bargain.

examples.ko: 오늘 횡재할 것 같은 느낌이 들어요.
examples.en: I have a feeling I'll get lucky today.
I got a movie ticket for free, so I think I hit the jackpot.

examples.ko: 횡재하고 싶다고 복권만 사면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't only buy lottery tickets just because you want a windfall.

explain: 애쓰지 않았는데 뜻밖에 돈이나 물건 같은 이득을 얻었을 때 써요. 그냥 '운이 좋다'보다 얻은 것이 눈에 보일 때 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '횡재했다!'처럼 기쁜 마음을 바로 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: You got it at half price? What a windfall!
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 뜻밖의 행운을 보고 놀라거나 축하할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to react with surprise or congratulations to someone else's unexpected luck.

phrases.example: 오랜만에 친구가 밥을 사 줘서 횡재한 기분이에요.
phrases.en: I feel like I hit the jackpot because my friend treated me to a meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 이득은 아니어도 뜻밖의 행운을 느낄 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works even for a small, unexpected piece of luck.
phrases.en_equiv: feeling like I struck it lucky

phrases.example: 이 가격에 이 가방이라니, 완전 횡재예요!
phrases.en: This bag at this price is a total steal!
phrases.nuance_ko: '횡재'를 명사로 쓴 말이에요. '완전'을 붙이면 대화체로 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 횡재 as a noun. Adding 완전 makes it sound conversational.

explain_en: Use it when you unexpectedly gain something like money or an item without trying hard. It fits better than just '운이 좋다' when there is a visible gain. In speech, people often exclaim it right away, like '횡재했다!'.
